current_evidence: The council's planning applications page links 'planning permission checklist' (downloads/file/7949, DOCX 92.47 KB) under both Home improvements and Commercial/residential developments, and searches found no newer Medway list; neither the page nor the download page shows a date.

issues.detail: The list is recorded as undated. That is defensible, because no adoption or update date appears on the planning page or the download page. However, the checklist dates back to a Cabinet adoption in 2011, and Grokbot's own extract says it is republished 'without consultation'. It also includes item 45 BNG (statutory from Feb 2024) and item 44 Fire Statement (Aug 2021), so it was last revised in or after 2024. The 'Outdated?' flag should note this instead of leaving the list simply undated.
issues.evidence: Medway Cabinet report 29 March 2011: 'The Cabinet is recommended to adopt the local validation checklists'; Grokbot tab item: 'As such, we republish our checklist without consultation.'
issues.grok_comment: Agree it shouldn't be left as undated, but the checklist itself gives a date: 'our validation checklist was reviewed in April 2025, and no changes to the local list was necessary'. The list date should be April 2025, not inferred from 2011/2024.
issues.claude_response: Kept, with a correction. The checklist says it was reviewed in April 2025, so that should be the list date (not undated).

issues.detail: Householder is recorded as '(none)', which is wrong. The council's page links this same checklist under 'Home improvements' ('view all requirements in our planning permission checklist'). Several items in it apply to all applications, including householders: Heritage Statement ('All applications involving a heritage asset or its setting'), Tree Survey ('within 5 metres of the crown spread of any tree'), Daylight/sunlight ('All applications where there is a potential adverse impact...'), Flood Risk Assessment ('flood zone 2 or 3 including minor development'), Photographs ('welcome photos on all application types'), and existing/proposed elevations and roof plans. Listed building consent is also recorded as '(none)', although the Heritage Statement item clearly applies to it.
issues.evidence: Planning applications page: checklist linked under 'Home improvements'; Grokbot's own excerpt '2) Heritage Statement When required? All applications involving a heritage asset or its setting.'

issues.detail: About 40 of the 47 Full-planning rows say 'INFERRED: application type not named ... placed under Full planning'. Examples are Heritage Statement, Tree Survey, Daylight/sunlight, Ecology Survey, Noise, Photographs, Ventilation/extraction and Lighting. These are general triggers that also apply to householder, outline, LBC and change-of-use applications. Meanwhile Outline, Reserved matters, LBC, s73 and Demolition in conservation area are all recorded as '(none)'.
issues.evidence: Grokbot notes column: 'INFERRED: application type not named in extracted text of a general local list; placed under Full planning'

issues.detail: 'Telecommunications supplementary information' is filed under 'Change of use - prior approval'. It belongs to telecoms prior approval (GPDO Part 16), not change of use. Flood Risk Assessment and Drainage Strategy were also put under Change of use prior approval only because the trigger text contains the words 'change of use'.
issues.evidence: Grokbot excerpt: '36) Telecommunications Developments - Supplementary information for Prior Approval applications'

issues.detail: Some requirement names do not match their trigger excerpts. 'Electric vehicle charging details' carries the Retail and town centre uses trigger. 'Sequential / Exception Test (flood)' carries the retail sequential-test text. 'Agricultural Land Classification / Soils' is only the landscaping-scheme sentence about a soil management survey, and no ALC requirement is shown. 'Planning Obligations / S106 Heads of Terms' carries the tail of the Affordable Housing item plus the Air Quality trigger.
issues.evidence: EV row excerpt: '33) Retail and town centre uses When required? Retail developments over 2,500sqm gross floorspace.'; Sequential row: 'if outside the town centres ... a sequential test is required.'

issues.detail: Several trigger excerpts are cut off, or start with the end of the previous item. Ecology Survey stops at 'Proposals that directly or indirectly affect;' and omits the list of what is affected. Planning Statement stops at 'Major applications and should include.' Design and Access Statement is a stray sentence ('Where no Design and Access Statement is required, it should be a stand-alone document') with no trigger. Parking reads 'points and parking provision.' Heritage Statement begins 'Drawn at a scale of 1:100 or 1:200.'

The capture is probably incomplete. Grokbot's own excerpts show the checklist is numbered 1) to 45), but only about 26 numbered items appear as requirements. Numbers 4, 7-9, 11-13, 15-17, 19-20, 23, 26, 28, 30, 41 and 43 are not represented. The excerpts also mention sub-items that were never captured, such as 'Road Safety Audit', 'Education or new resident/occupier information pack' (immediately before item 44) and 'Electrical charging point in car parks'. The source names of the missing items could not be confirmed because the DOCX could not be read.
issues.evidence: Excerpts: '...Education or new resident/occupier information pack 44) Fire Statement'; '...Road Safety Audit 38) Tree Survey'
issues.grok_comment: The capture is incomplete (e.g. 7 Accurate visual representations, 11 Protected Species, 13 Contaminated Land and 41 Waste Management Plans are missing). But some numbers on the 'missing' list are captured: 8 DAS, 15 Landscape/LVIA, 17 Viability Statement and 23 lighting scheme.
issues.claude_response: Partly accepted. Items 8, 15, 17 and 23 are captured. 7, 11, 13, 41 and others are still missing.

issues.detail: Some single source items are split into several rows with the same text. Item 22 appears as both Flood Risk Assessment and Drainage Strategy. Item 37 appears as both Transport Assessment and Travel Plan. One landscaping sentence appears as Landscaping scheme, Agricultural Land/Soils and Site levels. Item 33 appears as both Retail impact and EV charging.
issues.evidence: Identical trigger excerpts across those rows

issues.detail: Some tab items are process text, boilerplate or fragments rather than requirements. 'As such, we republish our checklist without consultation.' is filed under Local forms/checklists. The GDPR paragraph on third-party personal data is filed under Submission rules. A cut-off drawing-standards fragment reads 'A unique drawing number and title which also indicates any revisions (e.g.'.

summary: Grokbot's link is the only checklist the council publishes and appears to be current, but it is undated, and the DOCX could not be read to verify the contents. Grokbot's own excerpts show mismatched triggers, items that were probably missed (about 26 of 45 numbered items captured), and Householder and LBC wrongly recorded as having no local requirements.

withdrawn_issues.detail: Could not verify the contents independently. The link serves the file, a 92.47 KB DOCX, but WebFetch and the Google viewer both returned only binary data or a loading stub. Everything below comes from what the council's pages show and from inconsistencies inside Grokbot's own extracted text. A person needs to open the DOCX to finish the content check.
withdrawn_issues.evidence: WebFetch of the .docx returned '[binary data]'; download page: 'Planning permission validation checklist', DOCX, 92.47 KB, no date shown
withdrawn_issues.grok_comment: The DOCX text is readable: the raw copy (about 43k characters) has all of items 1) to 45). So the contents can be checked and the claims don't need to rest on Grokbot's excerpts alone.
withdrawn_issues.claude_response: Accepted. This was a note about what my helpers could not read, not a Grokbot error, so it is removed from the issue counts. The council stays on "Still to check by hand".
